selection_basis: Purposive small Python libraries with public test suites, no known mandatory GPU or external service. No main-cohort outcome, timing or repeat count has been inspected. This is not a representative random sample of Python repositories.
prior_exposure: The first 30 cachetools workflow runs were inspected during feasibility. They are exploratory pilot data. Blinker and all main candidates have not been queried for outcomes before this rule.
source_budget: At most 500 MB total source acquisition; no repository over 50 MB without revising this pilot plan. Preserve unavailable and oversized cases without favorable replacement.
api_rule: Collect the most recent 60 completed public GitHub Actions runs created no later than cutoff for each repository; retain all conclusions. Identify test-executing workflow definitions from source, independent of outcome. For the pilot use at most 20 chronological test requests; main sampling remains frozen before main measurements after pilot feasibility.
replay_scope: Replay public test-request source states under a newly pinned common runtime. This is a standardized replay, not reconstruction of original CI machines, secrets, dependency resolution or outcomes. Unavailable revisions and unsupported tasks remain counted.
identity_requirement: Repeated SHA or command text alone is not a cache hit. Reconstruct and hash actual input content, command and runtime and obtain the declared source-state qualification before reuse.
historical_request_policy: No extra unchanged requests are inserted into the observed-request replay. Controlled repeated handoffs are a separate experiment with separate denominators.
publication_requirement: Qualification evidence and elapsed AI-assisted operator time are recorded contemporaneously. Human qualification effort is not inferred. Positive full-workflow benefit may be claimed only for a fully measured deployment scope; remaining human effort is an explicit sensitivity variable.
